reasoning: Both sets use the same planning framework: one rllab package, an interface task, then spines, wiring and a final system task. The difference is in substance. A's RL design is stronger and more concrete. Snake gets a ladder of tabular Q-learning, then a DQN on the compact view, then a CNN on the full grid, with ablations of the memory, the target copy and exploration, plus a 1-D corridor that proves the shared core. The fish tank goes from REINFORCE to PPO, then to a school of fish, then to limited vision, with a stated claim that PPO beats REINFORCE. Predator-prey climbs from fixed opponents to naive co-learning to an opponent pool, with saved generations and a cross-play table. A also separates truncation from termination for correct bootstrapping. Its spec numbers are precise and its golden cases have concrete expected values, so A's packets can be built (for example, the Snake packet carries TC-01–TC-10 with exact boards). A's weaknesses are real. There is one very large milestone per stage. The S2 outline and CORE-06 still describe a 'deliberately revised' core, although AD-09/AD-13 adopt the batch-first, team-keyed core before M1 is built. Pipeline step tables list alternative classes as if they were steps. B splits its stages into more vertical milestones, and its method-check worlds are a good safety net. But B's M1 does not deliver the replay or a snake that clearly learns: the DQN spine is online Q-learning only, and both replay and SNAKE-08 are deferred to M2. B's M3 ('Check and explain') is carved off as a leftover milestone. Its spec is vaguer about the algorithms, and the predator-prey world moves to a square arena. Its golden cases are mostly property checks, and some packets omit types they need (Policy, ActionError, Settings). On balance A is the more trustworthy plan for learning RL.

strengths: Rich RL ladders in every stage: tabular → DQN → CNN with ablations; REINFORCE vs PPO; fixed → naive co-learning → pool self-play with cross-play ratings
Precise spec constants and concrete golden cases (exact boards, observation vectors, thresholds)
Batch-first, team-keyed core adopted before M1, so later stages need no rework
Context packets carry the types, invariants and oracles needed (e.g. M1-T13 carries TC-01–TC-10)
Reference comparison carefully mapped to Stable-Baselines3 defaults (AD-04, AD-10, AD-11)
weaknesses: One milestone per stage; M1 bundles the corridor, three agents, ablations, the reference, claims and replay, and M3 bundles three self-play rungs plus cross-play
Stale 'revised core' framing in the S2 outline and CORE-06, contradicting AD-09/AD-13
Pipeline step tables list alternative env/agent/baseline classes as sequential steps (PL-01 has 16 rows behind a 4-call entry)
Spec features tagged 'Stage: S1' (REF, BASE) now span all stages; BASE-01 is worded for Snake only

strengths: More vertical milestones; S2 is split into one fish → many fish → local sight along real dependency lines
The method-check world gate (TRAIN-06, AD-09) is a good guard against silent RL bugs
The paired permutation test with Holm correction is fully specified (EVAL-04)
Clear separation of pipeline entries in train/ versus cli/ (AD-10)
weaknesses: M1 delivers no replay and no snake that clearly learns; the DQN spine is online Q-learning with no buffer or target, and SNAKE-08 and replay are deferred
M3 'Check and explain the snake' is a leftover milestone (reference check plus write-up)
The spec names algorithms only generically; no tabular rung, no ablations, no explicit REINFORCE-vs-PPO lesson
Golden cases are mostly property or generator checks rather than exact oracles
Several single-step pipelines (watch, notes new, notes check) add structure with little content

A: M1-T31: real ladder runs depend on hyperparameter settings files (settings/**) that no packet specifies beyond defaults; the acceptance relies on tuning that is not described
B: M1-T08: packet lacks core.Policy (returned by policy()), the Settings type in MethodConfig, and the SpecMismatchError/NonFiniteError definitions it must raise; the WorldSpec sample is marked 'not written yet'
M1-T06: TC-06 is a generic property check with no exact boards; ActionError is referenced but not defined in the packet
